boundaries.label: Next.js server runtime — one Node process

cards.title: Request path
items: Server Actions are the primary mutation surface: 13 "use server" modules under src/lib/actions, each calling revalidatePath after a write.
Only 6 route handlers exist (/api/*), covering the file and read paths the browser needs directly: document upload/download, payslip preview/PDF, project report PDF and paginated employees JSON.
@react-pdf/renderer is lazy-loaded inside the two PDF handlers so the common serverless function graph stays small (src/app/api/payslips/[slipId]/pdf/route.ts:6-10).
next.config.ts sets Cache-Control: no-store on every /api/* response, so route handlers never serve a cached JSON payload.

cards.title: Data and money
items: PostgreSQL is the only store of record: 26 Prisma models spanning HR, payroll, projects, audit, notifications and email logs.
All money is integer paise — SalaryComponent.amountPaise, PayRun totals and StatutoryConfig thresholds — with formatting isolated in src/lib/money.ts.
PaySlip rows are immutable JSON snapshots written when a PayRun is finalized, so historic payslips never re-derive from current salary data.
The Prisma client is a lazy Proxy (src/lib/prisma.ts:48-52) so importing it during static prerendering never opens a connection.

cards.title: Auth and roles
items: Auth.js v5 Credentials provider bcrypt-compares the stored hash, then issues a 24h JWT carrying role, employeeId and companyId (src/auth.ts:26, 60-63, 84-101).
There is no middleware.ts: every server entry guards itself — AppShell calls requireAuth(), admin actions call requireAdmin(), and each route handler checks the session on its own.
The credentials callback reads User, Employee and Company from Postgres (src/auth.ts:53-70); the rest of the request then works from the JWT alone.
Account, Session and VerificationToken models exist for adapter-based sessions, but the configured JWT strategy has no adapter and never reads or writes them.

cards.title: External side effects
items: Resend is called synchronously inside the calling action (src/lib/services/email.ts:228); every attempt writes an EmailLog row that flips QUEUED to SENT or FAILED and can be retried from the email-logs screen.

Documents go to a private Vercel Blob on Vercel; elsewhere saveFile writes under UPLOAD_DIR or /tmp (src/lib/storage.ts:41-77). Disk fallback is deliberately disabled on Vercel because that filesystem is ephemeral.
@vercel/analytics is mounted in the root layout (src/app/layout.tsx:6, 29).
Punch-in/out, payroll, leave and notifications all resolve against the same Postgres tables — there is no queue, worker or cache anywhere in the runtime path.

cards.title: Notable gaps
items: checkRateLimit (src/lib/rate-limit.ts:13) is exported but has no callers — sign-in and document upload are unthrottled, and the limiter's own comment notes it only bounds one warm container.
The credential authorize path runs a bcrypt compare with no rate limit or lockout on the POST /api/auth/callback/credentials endpoint.
Email is fire-and-forget inside the request: a Resend outage marks the EmailLog FAILED but does not roll back the payroll or leave write that triggered it.
No background jobs, cron or webhook receivers exist, so month-close, payroll runs and reminders are all operator-initiated.
